issues.body:
crates/sparq-rsp/src/rspql.rs:757 declares `#[cfg(all(test, feature = "window-origin"))] mod window_origin_tests` (9 #[test] fns) and :855 declares `#[cfg(all(test, not(feature = "window-origin")))] mod window_origin_default_tests` (2 #[test] fns that assert the feature-OFF residual, e.g. that `T0 100 MAXDELAY 3` survives into the residual SPARQL and that the downstream PreparedQuery parse fails with a specific message).

This is exactly the detector's sensitivity criterion (b) (a cfg expression combining `test` and the feature in src/) and criterion (c) (the feature under `not()`), and it is the "compiled-out-assert" class research/feature-matrix-pyramid.md §2.1 calls unconditionally T2. `--enforce` should have hard-failed this demotion; it passes only because of the sanitizer defect (see the sparq-reason.yml issue).

Impact is total, not partial: the check tier runs `cargo clippy -p <crate> --features <F> -- -D warnings` with no `--all-targets` (.github/workflows/feature-matrix.yml), so these 11 tests are neither executed, nor compiled, nor linted on any PR. There is no workspace `--all-features` test lane (§1 premise correction 1), so nothing else runs them until push-to-main.
issues.fix_hint: Drop the `tier: "check"` line from the sparq-rsp (window-origin) leg so it stays a full T2 leg. If demotion is genuinely wanted, it requires an explicit reviewed `tier-reason:` override plus a written justification for abandoning per-PR coverage of the feature-OFF assertion brace — but given the cfg(not(...)) test module, the design record's own rule says this leg is not demotable.
issues.title: window-origin demoted despite cfg(all(test, feature)) AND cfg(all(test, not(feature))) test braces — ratchet criteria (b)+(c)

issues.body:
crates/sparq-reason/src/incremental.rs:845 contains `#[cfg(not(feature = "quoted-triples"))] crate::materialize_owl_rl(dict, &mut all);` paired with `#[cfg(feature = "quoted-triples")] crate::materialize_owl_rl_reify(...)` at :843 — two distinct closure-materialization paths selected by the feature.

Detector criterion (c) marks any `cfg(not(feature = F))` anywhere in the crate as SENSITIVE, and §4 states this is "deliberately over-inclusive: a distinct feature-OFF path means both states carry behavior worth executing". The leg should have hard-failed the ratchet.

The reason it did not is a defect in scripts/feature-matrix-tiers.py `_sanitize_for_cfg_scan`: the string-literal mask regex `b?"[^"\\]*(?:\\.[^"\\]*)*"` uses negated character classes that match newlines, and `_mask` replaces every interior character (newlines included) with `_`. Byte length is preserved — so the `assert len(safe) == len(content)` gives false confidence — but line structure is destroyed and real attributes inside the spurious span are erased. incremental.rs collapses from 3272 to 446 lines under sanitization and the attribute at :845 is blanked to spaces; rspql.rs collapses 884 -> 461. `_extract_cfg_expressions` consequently returns ZERO cfg expressions mentioning the feature for both files.

This makes the detector fail OPEN, contradicting its stated core invariant ("Any parse/IO/grep error classifies the leg SENSITIVE. A detector bug degrades to 'keep the full leg', never to a silent demotion") — there is no error raised at all, just silent erasure. The consequence is that `--enforce` passing is not evidence for ANY of the 19 demotions in this PR.
issues.fix_hint: Two parts. (1) Remove `tier: "check"` from the quoted-triples leg. (2) Fix the detector before re-attempting any flip: anchor string-literal masking per-line (or exclude newlines from the character classes, e.g. `[^"\\\n]`), blank comments BEFORE masking string literals rather than after, and handle raw strings (r#"..."#) which the docstring admits are unhandled. Add a regression test asserting the sanitizer is LINE-preserving (safe.count('\n') == content.count('\n')), not merely byte-length-preserving, and a fixture reproducing rspql.rs/incremental.rs so the two legs above classify SENSITIVE.
issues.title: quoted-triples demoted despite cfg(not(feature = "quoted-triples")) in src — ratchet criterion (c)

issues.body:
research/feature-matrix-pyramid.md §2.1 classifies sparq-vectors `compose` and `neuro-symbolic` as **b-module** (the feature gates a mod containing #[test] fns). §2's class table marks class B "Needs a per-PR build+test leg? **yes**", and §2.1's demotion list is explicit: candidates are 1 clear (sparq-py arrow) + 9 audit-pending b-coloc legs, and "Everything else (62): stays T2. No demotion, no re-litigating." sparq-reason `substrate-compare` (in sparq-reason.yml) is in the same b-module class and is likewise demoted here.

I confirmed the gated modules carry real unit tests that only exist when the feature is on: compose=9, verify(neuro-symbolic)=6, compare(substrate-compare)=12 #[test] fns. Because the module declaration itself is `#[cfg(feature = ...)]` in lib.rs, these compile to nothing in the default workspace lane — the feature-matrix leg was the only per-PR executor (the sq-vya1 rationale).

The detector cannot see this class at all: its criterion (b) only matches `cfg(all(test, feature))` in one expression or `#[cfg(feature)]` within 3 lines of `#[test]`. A feature-gated `mod` whose `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` sits inside is invisible to it. That is precisely why §8 requires a human per-test-body audit rather than relying on the ratchet.
issues.fix_hint: Revert the `tier: "check"` additions for compose, neuro-symbolic (this file) and substrate-compare (sparq-reason.yml), or attach the per-test-body audit evidence showing no gated test exercises behavior the default lanes already cover, recorded as a reviewed `tier-reason:` on each leg.
issues.title: Demotes b-module legs the design record places in "stays T2 — no demotion, no re-litigating"

issues.body:
Bead sq-s5dvo is specified in §8 as: "per-test-body audit of the 9 b-coloc legs (§2.1), then annotate **only audit-cleared legs (+ sparq-py `arrow`)** `tier: check`; mutation demo + before/after counts". §9 puts the ceiling at 10 legs demoted.

This PR demotes 19. Of those, only 5 are on the audit-pending b-coloc list (sparq-engine query-solution / params / explain-json / semijoin-bitmap, sparq-reason rif-xml). Three are b-module "stays T2" legs. The remaining 11 (sparq-core iri-fast, sparq-engine persistent-stats / templates, sparq-nlq query-policy, sparq-reason-diff rl-oracle, sparq-reason d-entail / rif-core / compiled-rules / quoted-triples, sparq-rsp window-origin, sparq-text highlight) post-date the §2.1 table and were never audited at all.

Conversely sparq-py `arrow` — the single "Clear (1)" demotion candidate, already `test: false` — is NOT demoted here.

The bead's required deliverables are also absent: the diff is fragments-only, with no audit record, no mutation demo, and no before/after leg counts. §8 flags this as "the only soundness-sensitive PR" in the chain precisely because the ratchet alone cannot justify it.
issues.fix_hint: Split this into the authorized flip plus a follow-up. Demote only audit-cleared b-coloc legs (+ sparq-py arrow), record the per-test-body audit for each in research/feature-matrix-pyramid.md with the mutation demo and before/after counts, and open a separate bead to audit the 11 legs added since the §2.1 table.
issues.title: Flip scope (19 legs) far exceeds the bead's authorized set (10), and omits the one cleared candidate

issues.body:
Across the 19 demoted legs, the feature-gated modules contain roughly 246 #[test] fns (measured on the head checkout): iri-fast 6, persistent-stats 2, query-solution 6, params 16, explain-json 6, semijoin-bitmap 11, templates 11, query-policy 3, rl-oracle 9, d-entail 35, rif-core 28, rif-xml 72, substrate-compare 12, quoted-triples 10, highlight 4, compose 9, neuro-symbolic 6, plus window-origin's 11.

Because each module is declared `#[cfg(feature = "F")] pub mod ...;`, none of these compile in the default workspace lane, and §1 (premise correction 1) confirms there is no workspace `--all-features` TEST lane. The demoted leg was therefore the sole per-PR executor.

Compounding this, the check tier runs `cargo clippy -p <crate> --features <F> -- -D warnings` with no `--all-targets`. §3 justifies dropping `--all-targets` on the grounds that "a demoted feature has no feature-gated test code by definition of the demotion criterion" — an assumption falsified by every leg above, and most starkly by window-origin. So the demoted legs lose test execution AND test-target compilation AND test-target lint per PR, leaving only the push-to-main backstop.

This may still be an acceptable trade for genuinely class-A legs, but it is a materially larger coverage reduction than the design record contemplated, and it is undocumented in the PR.
issues.fix_hint: Either add `--all-targets` to the check-tier clippy invocation so feature-gated test code is at minimum compiled and linted per PR, or narrow the demotion set to legs with genuinely zero feature-gated test bodies. Record the measured before/after test-execution delta in the design record as §10 requires, and confirm the sq-va7at demotion alarm is live before landing.
issues.title: ~246 feature-gated unit tests silently stop running per-PR; check tier omits --all-targets so they are not even compiled

issues.body:
Several demoted features gate security-relevant surfaces: sparq-nlq `query-policy` (parsed-algebra policy + result-form enforcement), sparq-engine `params` (parameterized prepared queries, the SPARQL-injection defense per sq-rp3um / #901), and sparq-reason `compiled-rules` (the scoped access-control N3 subset, sq-zgbso.3 / #1582).

Moving their test execution off the per-PR path to a post-merge backstop widens the window in which a regression in an injection-prevention or access-control path can be merged. params alone carries 16 gated unit tests.

This is not by itself a blocker — the push-to-main backstop still runs within minutes — but a change that relaxes per-PR verification on injection and access-control surfaces should say so explicitly rather than land as an unannotated one-line fragment edit.
issues.fix_hint: If these legs remain in the flip after the audit, add a `tier-reason:` on each security-relevant leg stating what still covers the injection/access-control path per-PR (e.g. named tests in the default workspace lane), so the trade-off is reviewable rather than implicit.
issues.title: Security-relevant features demoted without a stated risk note

verdict.summary:
This PR is the sq-s5dvo "demotion flip": it annotates 19 opt-in feature-matrix legs `tier: check`, moving them from full build+test to compile+clippy-only on pull_request/merge_group. The tier ratchet (feature-matrix-tiers.py --enforce) does pass — I ran it, 169 legs, 0 violations — but that green is not sound evidence, and two demotions are outright ratchet violations the enforcer misses due to a detector bug.

Verified against the head checkout:

1. sparq-rsp (window-origin) has `#[cfg(all(test, feature = "window-origin"))]` (rspql.rs:757, 9 tests) AND `#[cfg(all(test, not(feature = "window-origin")))]` (rspql.rs:855, 2 tests asserting feature-OFF behavior) — criteria (b) AND (c); the design record calls this class "unconditionally T2".

2. sparq-reason (quoted-triples) has `#[cfg(not(feature = "quoted-triples"))]` at incremental.rs:845 (two materialization paths) — criterion (c), which §4 calls "deliberately over-inclusive".

Root cause: `_sanitize_for_cfg_scan`'s string mask `b?"[^"\\]*..."` matches across newlines and replaces them with `_`. Byte length is preserved (so the internal assert holds) but line structure is destroyed and real attributes erased — rspql.rs collapses 884 lines to 461, incremental.rs 3272 to 446. Both sensitive attributes vanish before scanning, so the detector fails OPEN, contradicting its documented fail-closed invariant.

Scope also exceeds the bead: §8/§9 authorize the audit-cleared subset of 9 b-coloc legs plus sparq-py `arrow` (ceiling 10). This PR demotes 19, omits `arrow` (the one "clear" candidate), and includes 3 b-module legs §2.1 puts in "stays T2, no re-litigating". The required audit record, mutation demo and before/after counts are absent.
